Predict baseline risk of death

Source: R/predict.R
predict_baseline_risk.Rd

Adds each patient's linear predictor and predicted risk of death within 4 years with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) alone, called baseline risk.

Usage

predict_baseline_risk(newdata, model = mhspc_model())

Arguments

newdata

A data frame with one row per patient and one column per input listed by model_inputs(): ecog_ps (0, 1, or 2), gleason_score (2 to 10), visceral_metastasis (0 or 1, or logical), bone_metastases (a count, or a category code "0-3", "4-6", "7-10", or "11+"), psa (ng/mL), hemoglobin (g/L), albumin (g/L), alp (U/L), and ldh (U/L). Other columns are kept unchanged.

model

An mhspc_model object from mhspc_model().

Value

newdata with two columns added: linear_predictor, the model's risk score, and baseline_risk, the predicted 4-year risk of death as a proportion. Existing columns with these names are replaced.

Details

Inputs are checked first. Missing or invalid values stop with an error that names the row and input. Values outside the range in the trial data give a warning, because their estimates are extrapolations. Values above the upper cap used in model development are scored at the cap, with a message.

Examples

# Your own patient data: one row per patient, one column per input, plus any
# other columns, which are kept.
patients <- data.frame(
  patient_id = c("A", "B"),
  ecog_ps = c(0, 1), gleason_score = c(9, 9), visceral_metastasis = c(0, 0),
  bone_metastases = c(8, 15), psa = c(45, 150), hemoglobin = c(128, 115),
  albumin = c(41, 38), alp = c(180, 420), ldh = c(210, 280)
)
risk <- predict_baseline_risk(patients)
risk[c("patient_id", "baseline_risk")]
#>   patient_id baseline_risk
#> 1          A     0.6160547
#> 2          B     0.8956950
